title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 15th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en: Although the substance added by the actor in food production and operation is not on the "List of Non-edible Substances That May Be Illegally Added in Food" and the "List of Substances That May Be Illegally Added in Health Food" published by the relevant department of the State Council, if the substance has the same attributes as the substances listed in the above-mentioned lists, and based on relevant materials such as inspection reports and expert opinions, it can be determined that the substance has equivalent harm to the human body, it shall be identified as a "toxic or harmful non-food raw material" as stipulated in Article 144 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the 15th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2016] No. 449

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon discussion and approval by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the following eight cases (Guiding Cases No. 70-77), including the case of Beijing Sunshine Yibai Biotechnology Development Co., Ltd. and Xi Wenyou et al. for the production and sale of toxic and harmful food, are hereby issued as the 15th batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

December 28, 2016

Guiding Case No. 70

Beijing Sunshine Yibai Biotechnology Development Co., Ltd. and Xi Wenyou et al. v. — Production and Sale of Toxic and Harmful Food

(Approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on December 28, 2016)

Keywords: criminal / production and sale of toxic and harmful food / toxic and harmful non-food raw materials

Ruling Gist

If a perpetrator adds a substance during food production and operation that is not listed in the "List of Non-Edible Substances That May Be Illegally Added to Food" or the "List of Substances That May Be Illegally Added to Health Foods" published by the relevant department of the State Council, but the substance has equivalent attributes to those listed in the above lists, and, based on inspection reports and expert opinions and other relevant materials, it can be determined that the substance poses equivalent harm to the human body, it shall be recognized as a "toxic and harmful non-food raw material" as stipulated in Article 144 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 144 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The defendant Xi Wenyou registered and established Beijing Sunshine Yibai Biotechnology Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sunshine Yibai Company) in 2001 and was the actual person in charge of production and operation. Since 2010, the defendant unit Sunshine Yibai Company purchased raw materials for producing health foods from the defendant Tan Guomin at a price of RMB 600 per kilogram. These raw materials were processed by the defendant Tan Guomin after being purchased from the defendant Yin Lixin at a price of RMB 2,500 per kilogram. After purchasing the raw materials, Sunshine Yibai Company processed them into Sunshine Yibai brand Shanqi Shen Capsules, a health food for auxiliary blood sugar reduction, and sold them at a price of approximately RMB 100 per box to Jin Fuhai Health Food Store in Guangling District, Yangzhou City, and to multiple regions nationwide. The defendant Yang Lifeng was specifically responsible for production, and the defendants Zhong Limeng and Wang Hailong were responsible for sales. From May to September 2012, Shanqi Shen Capsules sold to Shanghai, Hunan, Beijing, and other places were detected to contain buformin hydrochloride. The food and drug regulatory authority informed Sunshine Yibai Company and Xi Wenyou of the test results. After learning the test results, the defendant Xi Wenyou immediately informed the defendants Tan Guomin and Yin Lixin. Despite knowing that the health products he produced and sold contained buformin hydrochloride, Xi Wenyou continued to purchase raw materials from Tan Guomin and Yin Lixin, and organized Yang Lifeng, Zhong Limeng, Wang Hailong, and others to produce and sell Shanqi Shen Capsules. After learning the test results, Tan Guomin and Yin Lixin continued to sell the raw materials to Xi Wenyou.

Buformin hydrochloride is the hydrochloride salt of buformin. Currently, buformin hydrochloride has not been approved for production or import by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council and may not be produced, sold, or used as a drug in China. An expert opinion issued by Professor Ge Xiaoqun of the Medical College of Yangzhou University and an appraisal opinion from the Judicial Appraisal Institute of Nanjing Medical University proved that buformin hydrochloride has a blood sugar-lowering effect, was withdrawn from the Chinese market long ago, and long-term use of health foods containing buformin hydrochloride may have adverse effects on the body and may even be life-threatening.

From late August 2012 until the case was uncovered in January 2013, the production and sales amount of Sunshine Yibai Company exceeded RMB 8 million. Among this, the amount of Shanqi Shen Capsules containing buformin hydrochloride that Xi Wenyou, Yin Lixin, and Tan Guomin participated in producing and selling exceeded RMB 8 million; the amount of Shanqi Shen Capsules containing buformin hydrochloride that Yang Lifeng participated in producing exceeded RMB 8 million; the amount of Shanqi Shen Capsules containing buformin hydrochloride that Zhong Limeng and Wang Hailong participated in selling exceeded RMB 400,000. Yin Lixin and Tan Guomin intentionally committed the crime together with Sunshine Yibai Company, constituting joint crime. Yin Lixin and Tan Guomin were aiders who provided toxic and harmful raw materials for the production and sale of toxic and harmful food, and both were accomplices in the joint crime. Xi Wenyou intentionally committed the crime together with Yang Lifeng, Zhong Limeng, and Wang Hailong, constituting joint crime. Yang Lifeng, Zhong Limeng, and Wang Hailong were accomplices who carried out the criminal acts of producing and selling toxic and harmful food under the direction of Xi Wenyou. Xi Wenyou played a principal role in the joint crime and was the principal offender. Yang Lifeng and Tan Guomin voluntarily surrendered after the crime and truthfully confessed the criminal facts, constituting voluntary surrender, and pleaded guilty voluntarily in court. Xi Wenyou, Yin Lixin, and Wang Hailong truthfully confessed the criminal facts after being apprehended and pleaded guilty voluntarily in court. Zhong Limeng truthfully confessed part of the criminal facts after being apprehended and voluntarily pleaded guilty to part of the criminal facts in court.

Judgment

The Guangling District People's Court of Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province, on January 10, 2014, rendered a criminal judgment (2013) Yang Guang Xing Chu Zi No. 0330: The defendant unit Beijing Sunshine Yibai Biotechnology Development Co., Ltd. was convicted of the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food and was fined RMB 15 million; the defendant Xi Wenyou was convicted of the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food and was sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for 3 years, and a fine of RMB 9 million; the defendant Yin Lixin was convicted of the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food and was sentenced to 12 years' imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for 2 years, and a fine of RMB 1 million; the defendant Tan Guomin was convicted of the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food and was sentenced to 11 years' imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for 2 years, and a fine of RMB 1 million; the defendant Yang Lifeng was convicted of the crime of producing toxic and harmful food and was sentenced to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 100,000; the defendant Zhong Limeng was convicted of the crime of selling toxic and harmful food and was sentenced to 4 years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 80,000; the defendant Wang Hailong was convicted of the crime of selling toxic and harmful food and was sentenced to 3 years and 6 months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 60,000; the illegal gains of RMB 8 million from the defendant unit Beijing Sunshine Yibai Biotechnology Development Co., Ltd., the illegal gains of RMB 671,500 from the defendant Yin Lixin, and the illegal gains of RMB 1.32 million from the defendant Tan Guomin were ordered to be recovered; the seized Shanqi Shen Capsules and granules containing buformin hydrochloride were ordered to be confiscated. After the judgment, the defendant unit and all individual defendants appealed. The Intermediate People's Court of Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province, on June 13, 2014, rendered a criminal ruling (2014) Yang Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 0032: The appeal was dismissed and the original judgment was affirmed.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that Article 144 of the Criminal Law provides: "Whoever mixes food produced or sold with toxic or harmful non-food raw materials, or knowingly sells food mixed with such raw materials, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years and/or a fine; if it causes serious harm to human health or has other serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years and a fine; if it causes death or has other especially serious circumstances, he shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 141 of this Law." Article 20 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases Involving Endangering Food Safety (hereinafter referred to as the "Interpretation") provides: "The following substances shall be recognized as 'toxic and harmful non-food raw materials': (1) substances prohibited by laws and regulations from being added or used in food production and operation activities; (2) substances listed in the 'List of Non-Edible Substances That May Be Illegally Added to Food' and the 'List of Substances That May Be Illegally Added to Health Foods' published by the relevant department of the State Council; (3) pesticides, veterinary drugs, and other toxic and harmful substances prohibited from use by announcements of the relevant department of the State Council; (4) other substances harmful to human health." Article 21 provides: "If it is difficult to determine 'sufficient to cause a serious food poisoning accident or other serious foodborne disease' or 'toxic and harmful non-food raw materials,' the judicial organs may make a determination based on inspection reports and combined with expert opinions and other relevant materials. When necessary, the people's court may notify relevant experts to appear in court to provide explanations in accordance with the law." In this case, buformin hydrochloride is a chemical substance that has not been approved for production or import by the drug regulatory authority in China and may not be produced, sold, or used as a drug in China; it is also not a food additive. Buformin hydrochloride also does not fall within the substances listed in Articles 20(2) and 20(3) of the above Interpretation. According to the expert opinion issued by Professor Ge Xiaoqun of the Medical College of Yangzhou University and the appraisal opinion from the Judicial Appraisal Institute of Nanjing Medical University, buformin hydrochloride has equivalent attributes and equivalent harm to the other hypoglycemic Western medicines (metformin hydrochloride, phenformin hydrochloride) listed in the "List of Substances That May Be Illegally Added to Health Foods" under Article 20(2) of the Interpretation. Long-term use of "Sunshine Yibai brand Shanqi Shen Capsules" containing buformin hydrochloride may pose a risk of toxic side effects to the human body, affecting human health or even endangering life. Therefore, buformin hydrochloride shall be recognized as a "toxic and harmful non-food raw material" as stipulated in Article 144 of the Criminal Law, in accordance with Articles 20(4) and 21 of the Interpretation.

The defendant unit Sunshine Yibai Company and the defendant Xi Wenyou, as the directly responsible person in charge of the production and sale of Shanqi Shen Capsules by Sunshine Yibai Company, and the defendants Yang Lifeng, Zhong Limeng, and Wang Hailong, as the directly responsible personnel for the production and sale of Shanqi Shen Capsules by Sunshine Yibai Company, knowing that the health food Shanqi Shen Capsules produced and sold by Sunshine Yibai Company contained buformin hydrochloride, a substance prohibited from being added by the state, still proceeded with production and sale; the defendants Yin Lixin and Tan Guomin, knowing that the raw materials they provided containing buformin hydrochloride, a substance prohibited from being added by the state, were used by the defendant Xi Wenyou to produce the health food Shanqi Shen Capsules for sale, still provided such raw materials to Xi Wenyou. Therefore, the above unit and individual defendants all lawfully constitute the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food. Among them, the acts of the defendant unit Sunshine Yibai Company and the defendants Xi Wenyou, Yin Lixin, and Tan Guomin constituted the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food. The act of the defendant Yang Lifeng constituted the crime of producing toxic and harmful food; the acts of the defendants Zhong Limeng and Wang Hailong constituted the crime of selling toxic and harmful food. Based on the circumstances and amounts of the crimes of the defendant unit and each defendant, and taking into account the role of each defendant in the joint crime, voluntary surrender, attitude of admitting guilt, and other sentencing circumstances, the above judgment was rendered.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Tang Yongmei, Chen Shengyong, Tang Junqi)

Guiding Case No. 71

Mao Jianwen v. — Refusal to Execute Judgment or Ruling

(Approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on December 28, 2016)

Keywords: criminal / crime of refusal to execute judgment or ruling / starting time

Ruling Gist

The time for "having the ability to execute but refusing to execute a judgment or ruling" begins from the effective date of the judgment or ruling. After a judgment or ruling with enforcement content becomes legally effective, a person with enforcement obligations who engages in acts of refusal to execute, such as hiding, transferring, or intentionally destroying property, thereby rendering the judgment or ruling unenforceable, if the circumstances are serious, shall be convicted and punished for the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 313 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The People's Court of Pingyang County, Zhejiang Province, on December 11, 2012, rendered a civil judgment (2012) Wen Ping Ao Shang Chu Zi No. 595, ordering the defendant Mao Jianwen to return to Chen Xianyin the investment capital of RMB 200,000 and interest that Chen Xianyin had placed under Mao Jianwen's name in Wenzhou Hongyuan Packaging Products Co., Ltd. within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment. The judgment became effective on January 6, 2013. Because Mao Jianwen failed to voluntarily perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument, Chen Xianyin applied for compulsory execution to the People's Court of Pingyang County on February 16, 2013. After the case was filed, during execution, the People's Court of Pingyang County discovered that on January 17, 2013, Mao Jianwen sold his Zhejiang CVU661 small ordinary bus for RMB 150,000 and used the proceeds for personal expenses, refusing to execute the effective judgment. Mao Jianwen was apprehended on November 30, 2013, and truthfully confessed the above facts.

Judgment

The People's Court of Pingyang County, Zhejiang Province, on June 17, 2014, rendered a criminal judgment (2014) Wen Ping Xing Chu Zi No. 314: The defendant Mao Jianwen was convicted of the crime of refusal to execute a judgment and was sentenced to 10 months' imprisonment. After the judgment was pronounced, Mao Jianwen did not appeal, and the prosecutorial authority did not file a protest. The judgment has become legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the defendant Mao Jianwen had the obligation to perform the execution obligations determined by the effective judgment. After the judgment or ruling with enforcement content of the people's court became legally effective, Mao Jianwen engaged in acts of refusal to execute, such as hiding and transferring property, thereby rendering the judgment or ruling unenforceable, and the circumstances were serious. His conduct constituted the crime of refusal to execute a judgment. The charge brought by the prosecutorial authority was established. Mao Jianwen truthfully confessed his crime after being apprehended, which may be considered for a lighter punishment.

The focus of dispute in this case was how to determine the starting time of the conduct of "having the ability to execute but refusing to execute" as stipulated in the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling; that is, whether the defendant Mao Jianwen's act of refusing to execute the judgment should be calculated from the date the relevant civil judgment became legally effective or from the date of filing for enforcement. In this regard, the court held that the entry into compulsory execution of an effective legal instrument is not a necessary element or prerequisite for constituting the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling. Mao Jianwen's act of refusing to execute the judgment should be calculated from the date the relevant civil judgment became legally effective on January 6, 2013. The main reasons are as follows: First, it conforms to the legislative intent. When the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress interpreted Article 313 of the Criminal Law, it pointed out that the "judgment or ruling of the people's court" in this article refers to a judgment or ruling that has enforcement content and has become legally effective in accordance with the law. This means that only after a judgment or ruling with enforcement content becomes legally effective does it have legal binding force and compulsory enforcement power, and the obligor has the responsibility to timely and actively fulfill the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument. The compulsory enforcement power of an effective legal instrument does not arise only after entering the compulsory execution procedure; it arises from the date the legal instrument becomes effective. Second, it is consistent with the Civil Procedure Law and its judicial interpretations. Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: If a litigation participant or another person refuses to perform a judgment or ruling of the people's court that has already become legally effective, the people's court may, depending on the severity of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law. Article 188 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: The conduct of refusing to perform a judgment or ruling of the people's court that has already become legally effective, as referred to in Article 111(1)(6) of the Civil Procedure Law, includes hiding, transferring, selling, or destroying property, or gratuitously transferring property, or trading property at an obviously unreasonable price, or abandoning due debts, or providing guarantees for others gratuitously, etc., after the legal instrument becomes legally effective, thereby rendering the people's court unable to enforce. Thus, the law clearly limits the conduct of refusal to execute to the period after the legal instrument becomes legally effective, and does not limit the subject of refusal to execute to the person subject to enforcement or the person obligated to assist in enforcement only after entering the compulsory execution procedure, nor does it limit the scope of adjustment of the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling to conduct that occurs only after the effective legal instrument enters the compulsory execution procedure. Third, it conforms to the legislative purpose. The legislative purpose of the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling is to solve the "difficulty of enforcement" of effective judgments and rulings of the court. Including the conduct of evading performance obligations between the effective date of the judgment or ruling and the filing of the case for enforcement within the scope of adjustment of the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling is the inherent meaning of the law in establishing this crime. Determining the effective date of the judgment or ruling as the starting time point for the conduct of refusal to execute in the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling can effectively urge the obligor, after the judgment or ruling becomes effective, to take the initiative to perform the obligations determined by the effective judgment or ruling under the deterrent force of criminal punishment, thus preventing effective judgments from becoming dead letters, so that the public truly respects judicial judgments, maintains legal authority, fundamentally solves the "difficulty of enforcement," and achieves the legislative purpose of the crime of refusal to execute a judgment or ruling.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Guo Chaohui, Zeng Hongning, Pei Lun)

Guiding Case No. 72

Tang Long, Liu Xinlong, Ma Zhongtai, and Wang Honggang v. Xinjiang Ordos Yanhai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Commercial Housing Sales Contract

(Approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on December 28, 2016)

Keywords: civil / commercial housing sales contract / loan contract / discharge of debt / legal effect / review

Ruling Gist

If the parties to a loan contract, after reaching a consensus through consultation, terminate the loan contract relationship and establish a commercial housing sales contract relationship, converting the principal and interest of the loan into a paid purchase price after reconciliation and accounting, this does not fall within the situation prohibited by Article 186 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, nor does the purpose of concluding such commercial housing sales contract constitute "providing a guarantee for a private lending contract" as stipulated in Article 24 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases. In the absence of circumstances as provided in Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, such a commercial housing sales contract has legal effect. However, with respect to the amount of principal and interest of the loan converted into the paid purchase price, the people's court shall, in combination with evidence such as the loan contract, conduct a review to prevent the parties from converting high interest exceeding the limits protected by law into the paid purchase price.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 186 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiffs Tang Long, Liu Xinlong, Ma Zhongtai, and Wang Honggang alleged: According to the contract agreed by both parties, Xinjiang Ordos Yanhai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yanhai Company) should deliver the houses that conform to the contract to the four individuals by September 30, 2014. To date, however, Yanhai Company has refused to perform the obligation of delivering the houses. Therefore, the plaintiffs requested the court to: 1. Order Yanhai Company to pay liquidated damages of RMB 60 million to Tang Long, Liu Xinlong, Ma Zhongtai, and Wang Honggang; 2. Order Yanhai Company to bear the losses and expenses of RMB 416,300 incurred by Tang Long, Liu Xinlong, Ma Zhongtai, and Wang Honggang in the process of asserting their rights; 3. Order Yanhai Company to bear all litigation costs of this case.

Yanhai Company defended: Tang Long, Liu Xinlong, Ma Zhongtai, and Wang Honggang should file separate lawsuits. The four individuals did not have the intent to purchase and sell housing with Yanhai Company; the housing sales contracts between the parties were in substance loans disguised as sales, and the commercial housing sales contracts served as security for the loan contracts. Such an arrangement violates Article 40 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 186 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, and is therefore invalid. The commercial housing sales contracts signed between the parties involved circumstances of gross unfairness and taking advantage of another's precarious position. The liquidated damages and loss expenses claimed by the four individuals also lack factual basis.

The court found upon trial: Tang Long, Liu Xinlong, Ma Zhongtai, Wang Honggang, and Yanhai Company entered into multiple loan contracts successively in 2013. Through actual lending and acceptance of assignment of claims from others, they acquired claims against Yanhai Company totaling RMB 260 million in loans. To secure performance of these loan contracts, the four individuals and Yanhai Company separately signed multiple advance-sale commercial housing contracts and registered them with the local housing property rights transaction management center. After these claims successively became due, as Yanhai Company failed to repay the loan principal and interest, the parties reconciled accounts and confirmed that Yanhai Company still owed the four individuals loan principal and interest totaling RMB 361,398,017.78. The parties then re-executed commercial housing sales contracts, agreeing that Yanhai Company would sell the housing under its name to the four individuals, and the aforementioned outstanding principal and interest would be converted into paid purchase price, with the remaining purchase price of RMB 38,601,982.22 to be paid in a lump sum to Yanhai Company after the completion of all property title transfer registration for the subject matter. The reconciliation statement submitted by Tang Long and the other three individuals with Yanhai Company showed that the loan interest between the parties was calculated at monthly rates of 3% and 4%, with overdue interest at 10%, and compound interest was also calculated.

Judgment

The High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, on April 27, 2015, rendered civil judgment (2015) Xin Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2, ordering: 1. Yanhai Company to pay Tang Long, Ma Zhongtai, Liu Xinlong, and Wang Honggang liquidated damages of RMB 9,275,057.23; 2. Yanhai Company to pay Tang Long, Ma Zhongtai, Liu Xinlong, and Wang Honggang legal fees of RMB 416,300; 3. Dismiss all other claims of Tang Long, Ma Zhongtai, Liu Xinlong, and Wang Honggang. The above amounts shall be paid in full within ten days after the judgment takes effect. After the judgment was pronounced, Yanhai Company appealed on the grounds that the sales contracts between the parties were security for the loan contracts, did not represent the true intent of the parties, and the amount owed included usurious interest. The Supreme People's Court, on October 8, 2015, rendered civil judgment (2015) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 180: 1. Set aside civil judgment (2015) Xin Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; 2. Dismiss all claims of Tang Long, Liu Xinlong, Ma Zhongtai, and Wang Honggang.

Reasoning

The effective court judgment held: Before the signing of the commercial housing sales contracts in dispute, there indeed existed a loan contract relationship between Yanhai Company and Tang Long and the other three individuals, and to perform the loan contracts, the parties signed corresponding advance-sale commercial housing contracts and registered advance-sale commercial housing notices. However, the commercial housing sales contracts in dispute were, under the circumstances where Yanhai Company had not repaid the loan principal and interest, renegotiated and reconciled, converting the loan contract relationship into a commercial housing sales contract relationship, converting the loan principal and interest into paid purchase price, and stipulating rights and obligations regarding housing delivery, balance payment, and liability for breach of contract. The creation, modification, and extinction of civil legal relationships, except as specially provided by law, require consensus through the manifestation of intent of the participants in the legal relationship. In civil transactions, changes in the manifestation of intent of the parties are not uncommon, and such changes in the manifestation of intent should be permitted unless prohibited by special provisions of law. In this case, the parties mutually agreed to terminate the loan contract relationship and establish a commercial housing sales contract relationship. This was not to provide security for the performance of the loan contracts between the parties, but rather, when Yanhai Company was unable to repay the debt upon maturity of the loan contracts, a transactional arrangement to balance the rights and obligations of both parties by selling Yanhai Company's commercial housing to Tang Long and the other three creditors. This transactional arrangement did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, did not fall within the circumstances prohibited by Article 186 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, and was also not subject to Article 24 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases. Respecting the parties' subsequent consensus on changing the nature of the legal relationship is inherent in implementing the principle of freedom of contract. Yanhai Company's claim that the commercial housing sales contracts in this case were invalid is not accepted.

However, while confirming that the commercial housing sales contracts are legally valid, since both parties admitted that the paid purchase price under the contracts was converted from the original loan principal and interest, and Yanhai Company argued that the amount of the debt included high interest. When a party requests judicial confirmation and protection of the purchaser's contractual rights, the people's court shall review the amount of loan principal and interest formed based on the actual performance of the loan contracts, to prevent parties from legalizing illegal high interest through signing commercial housing sales contracts or other means. Upon review, the method of calculating the loan interest between the parties exceeded the upper limit of interest protection for private loans stipulated by law. The amount of the debt containing high interest cannot be confirmed according to law. Since the legally protected loan interest rate is significantly lower than the loan interest rate confirmed by the parties' reconciliation, it should be considered that Tang Long and the other three individuals, as purchasers, have not fully paid the contractually agreed purchase price, and Yanhai Company's failure to deliver the housing within the agreed time should not be regarded as a breach of contract. The claim by Tang Long and the other three individuals for liquidated damages and legal fees based on Yanhai Company's alleged overdue delivery of housing constituting a breach of contract lacks factual and legal basis. The first-instance judgment erroneously ordered Yanhai Company to bear liability for paying liquidated damages and legal fees; this court hereby corrects this.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Xin Zhengyu, Pan Jie, Shen Dandan)

Guiding Case No. 73

Tongzhou Jianzong Group Co., Ltd. v. Anhui Tianyu Chemical Co., Ltd. — Dispute over the Right of Exclusion

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 28, 2016)

Keywords: Civil / Right of Exclusion / Priority Right to Compensation / Exercise Period / Starting Point

Ruling Gist

Where circumstances conform to Article 18 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, and a construction project construction contract is deemed terminated, the period for the contractor to exercise the priority right to compensation shall be calculated from the date of termination of the contract.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 286 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 18 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

In March 2006, Anhui Tianyu Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Anhui Tianyu Company) and Tongzhou Jianzong Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Tongzhou Jianzong Company) entered into a Construction Project Construction Contract, whereby Anhui Tianyu Company contracted out the civil works and installation works for the production area of its plant phase I project to Tongzhou Jianzong Company. The contract stipulated: commencement date: tentatively April 28, 2006 (subject to the actual commencement report), completion date: March 1, 2007, total contract period 300 calendar days. If the employer fails to pay the project payment as per the contract and no agreement on deferral of payment is reached, the contractor may stop work, and the employer shall bear liability for breach. Subsequently, the parties signed a Supplemental Agreement, which made new arrangements for the payment of project payment and stipulated a construction period of 113 days for the plant area and 266 days for the living area. On May 23, 2006, the supervision company issued a commencement order, Tongzhou Jianzong Company then organized construction, and by 2007, the main structures of the factory buildings in Anhui Tianyu Company's plant area were completed. Thereafter, because Anhui Tianyu Company failed to pay the project payment as contractually agreed, the work was halted, and the project has never been completed. On July 30, 2011, the parties reached a settlement agreement during arbitration, stipulating that when disposing of Anhui Tianyu Company's land and buildings to satisfy debts, Tongzhou Jianzong Company's project payment would have priority for compensation. Subsequently, as Anhui Tianyu Company was unable to pay its debts as they fell due, Jiangsu Hongyuan Construction Group Co., Ltd. applied to the Chuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province for Anhui Tianyu Company's bankruptcy and debt repayment. The Chuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, on August 26, 2011, rendered civil ruling (2011) Chu Min Er Po Zi No. 00001, ruling to accept the bankruptcy application. On October 10, 2011, Tongzhou Jianzong Company filed a claim with the bankruptcy administrator of Anhui Tianyu Company and asserted a priority right to compensation for the project. On July 19, 2013, the Chuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province rendered civil ruling (2011) Chu Min Er Po Zi No. 00001-2, declaring Anhui Tianyu Company bankrupt. On August 27, 2013, Tongzhou Jianzong Company filed a lawsuit requesting confirmation of its priority right to compensation for its claim.

Judgment

The Chuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, on February 28, 2014, rendered civil judgment (2013) Chu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00122, confirming that the plaintiff, Tongzhou Jianzong Group Co., Ltd., has a priority right to compensation for its declared claim concerning the civil works and installation works it performed on the production plant area of the defendant, Anhui Tianyu Chemical Co., Ltd. After the judgment was pronounced, Anhui Tianyu Chemical Co., Ltd. appealed. The High People's Court of Anhui Province, on July 14, 2014, rendered civil judgment (2014) Wan Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 00054, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective court judgment held: Although the construction project construction contract signed by the parties stipulated a time for project completion, the project in question was halted due to Anhui Tianyu Company's failure to pay the project payment as contractually agreed. There is no evidence that before the project halt and before the court accepted the bankruptcy application, the construction contract signed by the parties had been terminated or its performance had ceased, nor is there evidence that after the court accepted the bankruptcy application, the bankruptcy administrator decided to continue performance of the contract. According to Article 18 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China: "After the people's court accepts a bankruptcy application, the administrator has the right to decide to terminate or continue performance of contracts that were established before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application and that have not been fully performed by both the debtor and the other party, and shall notify the other party. If the administrator fails to notify the other party within two months from the date of acceptance of the bankruptcy application, or fails to reply within thirty days from the date of receiving the other party's reminder, the contract shall be deemed terminated." The construction project construction contract in question was actually deemed terminated after the court accepted the bankruptcy application, and the construction project in question could not be normally completed. According to the spirit of the summary of national civil trial work meetings of the Supreme People's Court, where the contract is terminated or its performance ceases after the contractual completion date due to the employer's reasons, the period for the contractor to exercise the priority right to compensation shall be calculated from the date of termination of the contract. Anhui Tianyu Company's claim that the time for exercising the priority right to compensation should be calculated from the contractually agreed completion date lacks basis and is not accepted. On August 26, 2011, the court ruled to accept the bankruptcy application for Anhui Tianyu Company. On October 10, 2011, Tongzhou Jianzong Company filed a claim with the bankruptcy administrator of Anhui Tianyu Company and asserted a priority right to compensation for the project payment. Therefore, the time when Tongzhou Jianzong Company asserted the priority right to compensation was October 10, 2011. Anhui Tianyu Company's argument that Tongzhou Jianzong Company's exercise of the priority right to compensation exceeded six months from the date of bankruptcy administration is inconsistent with the facts and is not supported.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Hong Ping, Hu Xiaoheng, Tai Wang)

Guiding Case No. 74

China Ping An Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Jiangsu Branch v. Jiangsu Zhenjiang Installation Group Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Insurer's Right of Subrogation

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 28, 2016)

Keywords: Civil / Insurer's Right of Subrogation / Property Insurance Contract / Damage to Insured Subject Matter by a Third Party / Breach of Contract

Ruling Gist

Damage caused to the insured subject matter of the insured by a third party's breach of contract may be deemed to fall within the circumstances of "damage to the insured subject matter by a third party" as stipulated in Article 60, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China. Where the insurer thereby exercises the right of subrogation against the third party in accordance with law, the people's court shall support it.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 60, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On October 28, 2008, the insureds, East China United Can Co., Ltd. (hereinafter East China Can Company) and East China United Can Second Co., Ltd. (hereinafter East China Can Second Company), and the defendant, Jiangsu Zhenjiang Installation Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Zhenjiang Installation Company), entered into a Construction Project Construction Contract, agreeing that Zhenjiang Installation Company would be responsible for the relocation and installation of the entire factory's machinery and equipment of the insureds. Part II "General Conditions" of the Construction Project Construction Contract, Clause 38, stipulates: "The contractor shall subcontract part of the contracted work in accordance with the provisions of the Special Conditions and shall enter into subcontracts with the subcontractors; without the consent of the employer, the contractor shall not subcontract any part of the contracted work"; "Subcontracting of work shall not relieve the contractor of any of its duties or obligations. The contractor shall assign appropriate management personnel to the subcontract site to ensure the performance of this contract. Any breach of contract or negligence by the subcontractor causing damage to the project or other losses to the employer, the contractor shall bear joint and several liability." Part III "Special Conditions" of the Construction Project Construction Contract, Clause 14, Item (1), stipulates: "The contractor shall not subcontract the construction of this project." "General Conditions" Clause 40 stipulates: "Before the start of construction, the employer shall arrange insurance for the life and property of its own personnel and third parties within the construction site and the construction site, and pay the insurance premiums"; "Materials and equipment to be installed that are transported to the construction site for use in the project shall be insured by the employer, who shall pay the insurance premiums"; "The employer may entrust the contractor with insurance matters, and the costs shall be borne by the employer"; "The contractor must arrange accident insurance for workers engaged in hazardous operations, and arrange insurance for the life and property of its own personnel within the construction site and for construction machinery and equipment, and pay the insurance premiums."

On November 16, 2008, Zhenjiang Installation Company and Zhenjiang Yamin Heavy Lifting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Yamin Transport Company) signed a Project Subcontract, subcontracting the equipment hoisting and transportation under the aforementioned contract to Yamin Transport Company. On November 20, 2008, with respect to the aforementioned entire factory relocation and equipment installation project, East China Can Company and East China Can Second Company purchased Installation Engineering All Risks Insurance from China Ping An Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Jiangsu Branch (hereinafter Ping An Insurance Company). The insurance proposal form recorded the insureds as East China Can Company and East China Can Second Company, and explicitly recorded that the contractor Zhenjiang Installation Company was not the insured. The "Material Loss Coverage Items and Insured Sums" column of the proposal form indicated: "Insured sum for installation items is RMB 177,465,335.56." Among the additional clauses, "Inland Transit Extension Clause A" was also insured, stipulating a compensation limit of RMB 2 million per incident for property loss. The insurance period was from November 20, 2008 to July 31, 2009. The proposal form was attached with a list of installed machinery and equipment, including: 2 units of SEQUA color printers, with a total original value of RMB 29,894,340.88. The insurance clauses attached to the proposal form provided the following explanation for "Inland Transit Extension Clause A": Both parties agree that, provided the insured has paid the additional premium as agreed, the insurance company shall be liable for compensating losses arising from natural disasters or accidents during inland transit, excluding water and air transport, of the insured property from the supply location within the People's Republic of China to the construction site specified in the insurance policy, provided the insured property has qualified packaging and loading during transit.

At approximately 10:30 a.m. on December 19, 2008, Jiang Yucai, driver of Yamin Transport Company, was driving a heavy semi-trailer truck (licenses Su LXXX69, Su LXX3 trailer) transporting the color printer from the old plant site to the new plant site. While turning, the steel cable on the vehicle broke, causing the color printer to tip over and slide to the ground, resulting in damage. After receiving the claim, Ping An Insurance Company prepared a list of damaged items. The Traffic Patrol Police Brigade of the Zhenjiang Public Security Bureau conducted an on-site investigation and determined that Jiang Yucai bore full responsibility for the accident. Subsequently, East China Can Company, East China Can Second Company, Ping An Insurance Company, Zhenjiang Installation Company, and Yamin Transport Company jointly entrusted Fanhua Insurance Surveyors and Adjusters Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Fanhua Company) to conduct an appraisal of the loss from the accident, and all agreed to accept the final adjustment result of Fanhua Company. On March 9, 2010, Fanhua Company issued an appraisal report, concluding: Cause of accident: equipment rolled over during transit (accident); policy liability established; total loss amount assessed: RMB 1,518,431.32, net loss: RMB 1,498,431.32; adjusted amount: RMB 1,498,431.32. Fanhua Company received RMB 47,900 in appraisal fees paid by Ping An Insurance Company.

On December 2, 2009, East China Can Company and East China Can Second Company sent a letter of claim to Zhenjiang Installation Company, stating: "All losses resulting from this accident shall be jointly borne by your company and Yamin Transport Company. Our party has reported the claim to the insured's Zhenjiang Central Sub-branch of Ping An Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Once the loss amount is determined, after the insurance company verifies and pays first, the rights within the compensation limit will be transferred by our party to the insurance company for exercise. For the portion insufficiently compensated, our party will separately pursue claims against your company and Yamin Transport Company."

On May 12, 2010, East China Can Company and East China Can Second Company issued a receipt for indemnity and a letter of transfer of rights to Ping An Insurance Company, stating: Received compensation of RMB 1,498,431.32 from Ping An Insurance Company. Agree to transfer all rights and interests of the insured subject matter for the above indemnified portion to Ping An Insurance Company, and agree that Ping An Insurance Company may pursue recovery from the liable party in the name of Ping An Insurance Company. Thereafter, Ping An Insurance Company filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting an order that Zhenjiang Installation Company pay compensation and appraisal fees.

Judgment

The People's Court of Jingkou District, Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, on February 16, 2011, rendered Civil Judgment (2010) Jing Shang Chu Zi No. 1822: 1. Jiangsu Zhenjiang Fitting Group Co., Ltd. shall pay Ping An Property Insurance Company of China, Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, RMB 1,498,431.32 within ten days after the judgment takes effect; 2. The claim of Ping An Property Insurance Company of China, Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, for payment of RMB 47,900 in appraisal fees was dismissed. After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Jiangsu Zhenjiang Fitting Group Co., Ltd. appealed to the Intermediate People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province. The Intermediate People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, on April 12, 2011, rendered Civil Judgment (2011) Zhen Shang Zhong Zi No. 0133: 1. Reversing the Civil Judgment (2010) Jing Shang Chu Zi No. 1822 of the People's Court of Jingkou District, Zhenjiang City; 2. Dismissing the claims of Ping An Property Insurance Company of China, Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, against Jiangsu Zhenjiang Fitting Group Co., Ltd. After the second-instance judgment was pronounced, Ping An Property Insurance Company of China, Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, applied for retrial to the High People's Court of Jiangsu Province. The High People's Court of Jiangsu Province, on May 30, 2014, rendered Civil Judgment (2012) Su Shang Zai Ti Zi No. 0035: 1. Reversing the Civil Judgment (2011) Zhen Shang Zhong Zi No. 0133 of the Intermediate People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province; 2. Affirming the Civil Judgment (2010) Jing Shang Chu Zi No. 1822 of the People's Court of Jingkou District, Zhenjiang City.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the focal issues in this case were: 1. Whether the scope of application of the insurer's subrogation right is limited to the right to claim damages for tort; 2. Whether Zhenjiang Fitting Company could refuse the insurer's exercise of the subrogation right on the grounds that East China Canning Company and East China Canning Second Company had already purchased property loss insurance.

Regarding the first issue. Article 60, paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Insurance Law) provides: "Where an insured event is caused by a third party's damage to the subject matter insured, the insurer, from the date of paying the insurance proceeds to the insured, may exercise the insured's right to claim compensation from the third party within the amount of compensation." This paragraph uses the expression "damage to the subject matter insured by a third party causes the insured event" and does not restrict it to "damage by tort of a third party to the subject matter insured causes the insured event." There is no legal basis for interpreting the scope of the insurer's subrogation right as limited to the right to claim damages for tort. From a legislative purpose perspective, the provision of the insurer's subrogation right system is intended to prevent the insured of property insurance from receiving compensation from both the insurer and the third party due to the insured event, thereby obtaining undue benefits exceeding actual losses, and increasing moral hazard. Interpreting "damage" in Article 60, paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law as referring only to "tort damage" does not conform to the purpose of establishing the insurer's subrogation right system. Therefore, the insurer's exercise of the subrogation right should be premised on the insured having a right to claim damages against the third party. The right to claim compensation here may arise from the third party's tortious act against the subject matter insured, or from the third party's breach of contract, etc., and should not be limited to the right to claim compensation for tort. In this case, Ping An Insurance Company exercised its subrogation right based on Zhenjiang Fitting Company's breach of contract, not tort. Whether Zhenjiang Fitting Company had fault regarding the occurrence of the insured event does not affect the handling of the case. Moreover, the Construction Project Construction Contract stipulated that "the contractor shall not subcontract the project." Therefore, Zhenjiang Fitting Company's defense that it should not bear responsibility because it had no fault regarding the insured event is untenable. Ping An Insurance Company's claim against Zhenjiang Fitting Company is proper in terms of subject qualification and is not improper.

Regarding the second issue. Zhenjiang Fitting Company argued that in the general terms of the construction project construction contract between the developer and it, Article 40 stipulated that the equipment to be installed would be insured by the developer, who would pay the insurance premium. From this stipulation, it could be seen that regarding the factory relocation and equipment disassembly and installation matters, the developer and Zhenjiang Fitting Company jointly agreed to handle the insurance. Although the insurance premium was borne by the developer, this agreement was reflected in the contract terms between the parties, that is, the cost was borne by both parties, or, Zhenjiang Fitting Company had made concessions on the insurance cost in the total contract price. In the insurance business underwritten by the developer with Ping An Insurance Company, the contractor should also be the insured. Regarding the above defense of Zhenjiang Fitting Company, Article 12, paragraphs 2 and 6 of the Insurance Law respectively provide: "The insured of property insurance shall have an insurable interest in the subject matter insured at the time of the insured event"; "Insurable interest refers to the interest legally recognized by the insured or the policyholder in the subject matter insured." Accordingly, different entities may have different insurable interests in the same subject matter insured, may insure different types of insurance corresponding to their insurable interests for the same subject matter, establish different insurance contracts, and obtain insurance coverage within their respective scopes of insurable interests, thereby achieving the purpose of using the insurance system to disperse their respective risks. Because the developer and the contractor have different insurable interests in the subject matter insured, only by separately purchasing property insurance categories corresponding to their insurable interests can they obtain corresponding insurance coverage; the two cannot substitute for each other. As the owners of the subject matter insured, the developer East China Canning Company and East China Canning Second Company purchased installation works all risks insurance based on the ownership insurable interest in the subject matter, aimed at spreading the risk of damage or loss of the subject matter, and is property loss insurance in nature; the additional "Inland Transit Extension Clause A" purchased provides that "the insurance company is liable for losses caused by natural disasters or accidents during inland transit, excluding water and air transport, from the supply location within the People's Republic of China to the worksite specified in the insurance policy." This additional insurance is also property loss insurance in nature. Zhenjiang Fitting Company is not the owner of the subject matter insurance in this case, does not have the ownership insurable interest, and as a contractor, it has a liability insurance interest in the subject matter insurance. If it wishes to transfer the liability for damages that may arise during the construction process to the insurer, it should purchase relevant liability insurance, and cannot use the property loss insurance purchased by the developer to exempt itself from the liability for damages it should bear. Secondly, the developer did not recognize the contractor's status as an insured. The insured recorded in the Application Form for Installation Works All Risks Insurance in this case were East China Canning Company and East China Canning Second Company, and it was clearly recorded that the contractor, Zhenjiang Fitting Company, was not the insured. Therefore, Zhenjiang Fitting Company's defense that "in the insurance business underwritten by the developer with Ping An Insurance Company, the contractor should also be the insured" is untenable. The Construction Project Construction Contract clearly stipulates that "materials and equipment to be installed that are transported to the construction site shall be insured by the developer, who will pay the insurance premium" and "project subcontracting cannot relieve the contractor of any responsibilities or obligations. Any breach of contract or negligence by the subcontractor causing damage to the project or other losses to the developer, the contractor shall bear joint liability." It can be seen that the developer never intended to exempt the contractor from liability for damages within the scope of insurance compensation, and the parties did not agree to exempt the contractor from liability for damages within the scope of insurance compensation. Thirdly, after the insured event occurred, the insured actively claimed against the contractor and issued a subrogation receipt to Ping An Insurance Company. Based on the above circumstances, Zhenjiang Fitting Company's claim that it also had an insurable interest in the subject matter insurance and that the owners of the subject matter insurance, East China Canning Company and East China Canning Second Company, had already purchased property loss insurance, to exempt itself from liability for breach of contract damages that it should bear against the two canning companies under the construction project construction contract, and further to refuse Ping An Insurance Company's exercise of subrogation right, has no legal basis and is not supported.

Based on the above reasoning, the judgment was rendered as above.

(Trial judges of the effective judgment: Liu Zhen, Cao Xia, Ma Qian)

Guiding Case No. 75

China Biodiversity Conservation and Green Development Foundation v. Ningxia Ruitai Technology Co., Ltd. — Environmental Pollution Public Interest Litigation

(Approved by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court for discussion, released on December 28, 2016)

Keywords Civil / Environmental pollution public interest litigation / Social organization specialized in environmental protection public interest activities

Ruling Gist

1. Where a social organization's articles of association do not explicitly state the maintenance of environmental public interest, but its work content falls within the scope of protecting environmental elements and ecosystems, it shall be deemed to comply with Article 4 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation), which stipulates that "the purpose and main business scope determined by the social organization's articles of association are to maintain the public interest."

2. The "environmental protection public interest activities" specified in Article 4 of the Interpretation include not only actions that directly improve the ecological environment, but also activities related to environmental protection that are conducive to improving the environmental governance system, enhancing environmental governance capacity, and promoting broad consensus on environmental protection in society.

3. Where the matter sued by a social organization corresponds to its purpose and business scope, or has a certain connection with the environmental elements or ecosystems it protects, it shall be deemed to comply with Article 4 of the Interpretation, which stipulates "relevance to its purpose and business scope."

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On August 13, 2015, China Biodiversity Conservation and Green Development Foundation (hereinafter referred to as the Green Development Foundation) filed a lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, alleging: Ningxia Ruitai Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ruitai Company) illegally discharged excessive wastewater directly into evaporation ponds during its production process, causing serious pollution to the Tengger Desert, and as of the time of filing the lawsuit, had not yet completed rectification. It requested a judgment ordering Ruitai Company to: (1) cease the illegal pollution behavior; (2) eliminate the danger caused by environmental pollution; (3) restore the ecological environment or establish a special fund for desert environment restoration and entrust a qualified third party to carry out restoration; (4) for the second and third requests, the court should organize the plaintiff, technical experts, legal experts, people's congress deputies, and CPPCC members to jointly accept the results; (5) compensate for ecological function losses before environmental restoration; (6) publish a public apology in national media, etc.

The Green Development Foundation submitted its foundation legal person registration certificate to the court, showing it is a foundation legal person registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs of the People's Republic of China. The Green Development Foundation also submitted inspection materials from 2010 to 2014, showing it had passed annual inspections for the five years prior to filing this public interest litigation. The Green Development Foundation also submitted a declaration of no illegal record, stating it had not received any administrative or criminal penalties for violating laws or regulations in engaging in business activities within the past five years. Additionally, the Green Development Foundation's articles of association stipulate that its purpose is "to extensively mobilize the whole society to care about and support the cause of biodiversity conservation and green development, protect national strategic resources, promote ecological civilization construction and harmony between man and nature, and build a better home for mankind." During the first instance, second instance, and retrial of the case, the Green Development Foundation submitted to the court relevant evidence materials showing that since its establishment in 1985, it has been continuously engaged in activities including holding environmental protection seminars, organizing ecological investigations, conducting environmental protection publicity and education, and filing environmental civil public interest lawsuits.

Judgment

The Intermediate People's Court of Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, on August 19, 2015, rendered Civil Ruling (2015) Wei Min Gong Li Zi No. 6, ruling that the Green Development Foundation could not be identified as a social organization "specialized in environmental protection public interest activities" as stipulated in Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Environmental Protection Law), and therefore ruled not to accept the Green Development Foundation's lawsuit. The Green Development Foundation appealed to the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. That court, on November 6, 2015, rendered Civil Ruling (2015) Ning Min Gong Li Zhong Zi No. 6, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original ruling. The Green Development Foundation then applied for retrial to the Supreme People's Court. The Supreme People's Court, on January 22, 2016, rendered Civil Ruling (2015) Min Shen Zi No. 3377, ruling to bring the case up for trial; and on January 28, 2016, rendered Civil Ruling (2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 47, ruling that the case should be accepted by the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that this case is an environmental pollution public interest litigation initiated by a social organization. The focal issue in this case is whether the Green Development Foundation should be identified as a social organization specialized in environmental protection public interest activities.

Article 55 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China establishes the system of environmental civil public interest litigation, explicitly stating that agencies prescribed by law and relevant organizations may initiate environmental public interest litigation. Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law provides: "For conduct that pollutes the environment or damages ecosystems and harms the public interest, social organizations that meet the following conditions may file a lawsuit with the people's court: (1) they are lawfully registered with the civil affairs department of the people's government at or above the city level with districts; (2) they have specialized in environmental protection public interest activities for at least five consecutive years and have no record of illegal activities. Social organizations that meet the conditions set forth in the preceding paragraph may file a lawsuit with the people's court, and the people's court shall accept the case in accordance with the law." Article 4 of the Interpretation further clarifies the criteria for determining whether a social organization is "specialized in environmental protection public interest activities," i.e., "a social organization whose articles of association determine its purpose and main business scope as maintaining the public interest and that engages in environmental protection public interest activities may be identified as a social organization 'specialized in environmental protection public interest activities' as stipulated in Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law. The social public interest involved in the lawsuit filed by the social organization shall be related to its purpose and business scope." Regarding whether the Green Development Foundation can file this lawsuit as a social organization "specialized in environmental protection public interest activities," the examination should focus on three aspects: whether its purpose and business scope include maintaining environmental public interest, whether it actually engages in environmental protection public interest activities, and whether the environmental public interest it seeks to maintain is related to its purpose and business scope.

I. Whether the purpose and business scope stipulated in the Green Development Foundation's articles of association include maintaining environmental public interest. The common interest enjoyed by the public in surviving and developing in a healthy, comfortable, and beautiful environment takes various forms. Whether a social organization's purpose and business scope include maintaining environmental public interest should be determined based on its content, not simply by its literal expression. Even if the social organization's articles of association do not explicitly state the maintenance of environmental public interest, if its work content falls within the scope of protecting various natural factors that affect human survival and development, whether natural or artificially modified, including the protection of environmental elements such as the atmosphere, water, oceans, land, mineral deposits, forests, grasslands, wetlands, wild organisms, natural relics, cultural relics, nature reserves, scenic spots, cities and villages, and their ecosystems, it can be deemed that the purpose and business scope include maintaining environmental public interest.

The United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity, which China signed in 1992, states that biological diversity means the variability among living organisms from all sources including, inter alia, terrestrial, marine and other aquatic ecosystems and the ecological complexes of which they are part; this includes diversity within species, between species and of ecosystems. Article 30 of the Environmental Protection Law provides: "Exploitation of natural resources shall be carried out in a reasonable manner to protect biological diversity, ensure ecological security, and formulate and implement relevant plans for ecological protection and restoration in accordance with the law. The introduction of alien species, as well as the research, development and utilization of biotechnology, shall take measures to prevent damage to biological diversity." It can be seen that biodiversity conservation is an important part of environmental protection and also constitutes an important component of maintaining environmental public interest.

The Green Development Foundation's articles of association explicitly stipulate that its purpose is "to extensively mobilize the whole society to care about and support the cause of biodiversity conservation and green development, protect national strategic resources, promote ecological civilization construction and harmony between man and nature, and build a better home for mankind," which meets the requirements of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity and the Environmental Protection Law for protecting biodiversity. At the same time, "promoting ecological civilization construction," "harmony between man and nature," and "building a better home for mankind" are in line with the concept of green development and are closely related to environmental protection, falling within the scope of maintaining environmental public interest. Therefore, it should be determined that the Green Development Foundation's purpose and business scope include maintaining environmental public interest.

II. Whether the Green Development Foundation actually engages in environmental protection public interest activities. Environmental protection public interest activities include not only actions that directly improve the ecological environment, such as tree planting, endangered species protection, energy conservation and emission reduction, and environmental restoration, but also activities related to environmental protection, such as publicity and education, research and training, academic exchanges, legal aid, and public interest litigation, which are conducive to improving the environmental governance system, enhancing environmental governance capacity, and promoting broad consensus on environmental protection in society. The relevant evidence materials submitted by the Green Development Foundation during the first instance, second instance, and retrial of this case, including its history, photos of public interest activities, and case acceptance notices for environmental public interest lawsuits, although not subject to cross-examination during the examination for case acceptance stage, sufficiently show that since its establishment in 1985, the Green Development Foundation has been continuously engaged in environmental protection activities for a long time, including holding environmental protection seminars, organizing ecological investigations, conducting environmental protection publicity and education, and filing environmental civil public interest lawsuits, which complies with the provisions of the Environmental Protection Law and the Interpretation. At the same time, the above evidence also proves that the Green Development Foundation has been engaged in environmental protection public interest activities for at least five years, meeting the requirement of Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law that social organizations engaged in environmental protection public interest activities should have been doing so for five years or more.

III. Whether the social public interest involved in this case is related to the Green Development Foundation's purpose and business scope. According to Article 4 of the Interpretation, the environmental public interest involved in a public interest lawsuit filed by a social organization should have a certain connection with the social organization's purpose and business scope. This provision is intended to ensure that the environmental public interest protection matters sued by the social organization correspond to or are related to its purpose and business scope, thereby ensuring that the social organization has the corresponding litigation capacity. Therefore, even if the matter sued by the social organization does not correspond to its purpose and business scope, if it has a certain connection with the environmental elements or ecosystems it protects, its subject qualification should still be confirmed based on the relevance standard. This environmental public interest lawsuit is directed at pollution of the Tengger Desert. The complex and fragile desert ecosystem formed by the interaction of desert biological communities and their environment requires even more careful use and dedicated care by humanity. The Green Development Foundation alleged that Ruitai Company discharged excessive wastewater into evaporation ponds, severely damaging the already fragile ecosystem of the Tengger Desert, and the maintenance of the environmental public interest involved falls within the purpose and business scope of the Green Development Foundation.

In addition, the registration certificate for a foundation legal person submitted by CBDG shows that CBDG is a foundation legal person registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs of the PRC. The annual inspection certification materials for 2010 to 2014 submitted by CBDG indicate that its annual inspections for the five years prior to filing this public interest litigation were all qualified. CBDG also submitted, in accordance with Article 5 of the Interpretation, a declaration of no illegal record stating that it had not been subject to administrative or criminal penalties for violating laws or regulations in the course of its business activities within the preceding five years. Accordingly, CBDG also meets the other requirements for social organizations to initiate environmental public interest litigation under Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law, and Articles 2, 3, and 5 of the Interpretation, and therefore has the standing to initiate civil environmental public interest litigation.

(Judges of the Effective Judgment: Liu Xiaofei, Wu Kaimin, Ye Yang)

Guiding Case No. 76

Pingxiang Yapeng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Pingxiang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources — dispute over non-performance of an administrative agreement

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, Released on December 28, 2016)

Keywords: administrative / administrative agreement / contract interpretation / judicial review / legal effect

Ruling Gist

An interpretation of the terms of an administrative agreement given by an administrative organ within the scope of its functions and powers is legally binding on both parties to the agreement. After review, the people's court may, based on the actual circumstances, use such interpretation as a basis for reviewing the administrative agreement.

Related Legal Provision

Article 12 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC

Basic Facts

On January 13, 2004, the Pingxiang Land Acquisition and Reserve Center, entrusted by the Pingxiang Meat Joint Processing Plant and with the approval of the defendant, the Pingxiang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources (hereinafter referred to as the Municipal Land Bureau), published an announcement in the Pingxiang Daily for an open auction of the right to use state-owned land. The auction was scheduled to be held at the Land Transaction Hall from January 30, 2004, to February 12, 2004, for the parcel TG-0403, located at Wangongtang, Houbu Street, Anyuan District, Pingxiang City. The land transfer area was 23,173.3 square meters, the development land was for commercial and residential mixed use, the cold storage workshop was to maintain the status quo, the floor area ratio was 2.6, and the land use term was 50 years. Pingxiang Yapeng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yapeng Company) obtained the state-owned land use right for parcel TG-0403 through bidding and auction on February 12, 2006, at a price of RMB 7.68 million, and signed the State-owned Land Use Right Transfer Contract with the defendant Municipal Land Bureau on February 21, 2006. The contract stipulated that the purpose of the transferred land was commercial and residential mixed use, with the cold storage workshop maintaining the status quo. The land transfer fee was RMB 331.42 per square meter, totaling RMB 7.68 million. On March 2, 2006, the Municipal Land Bureau issued two state-owned land use certificates to Yapeng Company: Ping Guo Yong (2006) No. 43750 and Ping Guo Yong (2006) No. 43751. The land use type in the certificate No. 43750 was industrial, the use right type was transfer, and the use right area was 8,359 square meters; the land use type in certificate No. 43751 was commercial and residential mixed use. Regarding this, Yapeng Company argued that the stipulation "the cold storage workshop maintains the status quo" meant maintaining the functional use of the cold storage, not maintaining the nature of the land use type, and requested that the land use type in one of the certificates be corrected from "industrial" to "commercial and residential mixed use." However, the Municipal Land Bureau maintained that maintaining the status quo meant that the cold storage workshop was transferred with an industrial land use nature, and that Yapeng Company had paid the land transfer fee based on the cold storage workshop being industrial land, and therefore refused to correct the land use purpose. On July 30, 2012, the Pingxiang Municipal Planning Bureau issued a reply to the Pingxiang Land Acquisition and Reserve Center regarding the interpretation of certain issues in the "Letter on the Parcel of the Pingxiang Meat Joint Processing Plant," the main contents of which were: Our bureau clearly stated in the planning conditions issued on October 8, 2003, that the land use nature of the parcel was commercial and residential mixed use (with the cold storage workshop area approximately 7,300 square meters, similarly hereinafter), but the cold storage workshop was to maintain the status quo. According to the regulatory detailed planning for the parcel, its land use nature was residential (compatible with commercial). However, since the food cold storage workshop on the parcel is currently the only agricultural product reserve and preservation warehouse in the city and an important livelihood project, the functional use of the approximately 7,300 square meter cold storage on the parcel is temporarily retained and shall not be demolished without approval from the government or relevant competent authorities. On February 21, 2013, the Municipal Land Bureau gave a written reply to Yapeng Company: 1. Based on the planning conditions issued by the Municipal Planning Bureau and the actual situation of the parcel, we agree to your company's application to change the land use purpose of the cold storage workshop land in parcel TG-0403 from industrial land to commercial and residential land. 2. Since your company obtained the use right for the cold storage workshop land in this parcel at the price of industrial land, pursuant to the provisions of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC, your company's application to change the land use purpose of the cold storage workshop land in parcel TG-0403 from industrial land to commercial and residential land requires the supplementary payment of the land transfer fee.
