The supplementary land transfer fee may be calculated as the assessed value of the parcel at the time of transfer for mixed use (residential, office) minus an equal proportion, i.e., RMB 2,976,560 * 70% = RMB 2,083,600. 3. After the adjustment of the land use purpose for the cold storage workshop land, its functional use may not be changed without approval from the municipal government. On March 10, 2013, Yapeng Company filed an administrative lawsuit with the court, requesting that the defendant be ordered to correct the land use type in the state-owned land use certificate Ping Guo Yong (2006) No. 43750 from "industrial" to "commercial and residential mixed use (cold storage workshop maintains the status quo)" and to revoke the decision in item 2 of the defendant's "Reply on Issues Concerning the Land Use Purpose of Parcel TG-0403 for Yapeng Real Estate Co., Ltd." regarding the supplementary payment of the land transfer fee of RMB 2,083,600.

Judgment

The Anyuan District People's Court of Pingxiang, Jiangxi Province, rendered administrative judgment (2014) An Xing Chu Zi No. 6 on April 23, 2014: 1. The defendant, Pingxiang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, shall, within ninety days from the effective date of this judgment, correct the land use purpose of the 8,359.1 square meters in the state-owned land use certificate Ping Guo Yong (2006) No. 43750 in accordance with the law. 2. Revoke the decision in item 2 of the "Reply on Issues Concerning the Land Use Purpose of Parcel TG-0403 for Yapeng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." issued by the defendant Pingxiang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources on February 21, 2013, regarding the supplementary payment of the land transfer fee of RMB 2,083,600. After the judgment was announced, Pingxiang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources appealed. The Pingxiang Intermediate People's Court of Jiangxi Province rendered administrative judgment (2014) Ping Xing Zhong Zi No. 10 on August 15, 2014: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: An administrative agreement is an agreement concluded between an administrative organ, in order to achieve a public interest or administrative objective, within the scope of its statutory duties, and a citizen, legal person, or other organization, which contains administrative law rights and obligations. The administrative agreement in this case is the state-owned land use right transfer contract signed between the Municipal Land Bureau, on behalf of the state, and Yapeng Company. Administrative agreements emphasize good faith, equality, and voluntariness. Once signed, all parties must strictly abide by them. Without legitimate reasons, an administrative organ may not impose additional obligations on the other party beyond the agreement or unilaterally modify or terminate it. In this case, the land use purpose publicly announced for the transfer of parcel TG-0403 was "development land for commercial and residential mixed use, cold storage workshop maintaining the status quo," and the transfer contract stipulated "the purpose of the transferred land is commercial and residential mixed use, cold storage workshop maintaining the status quo." However, the Municipal Land Bureau and Yapeng Company had a disagreement on the understanding of this stipulation. The Pingxiang Municipal Planning Bureau, in its reply to the former Pingxiang Meat Joint Processing Plant, confirmed that the land use nature of the total area of 23,173.3 square meters (including the cold storage workshop) for the state-owned land use right of parcel TG-0403 was commercial and residential mixed use. The interpretation by the Pingxiang Municipal Planning Bureau was consistent with the land use purpose clearly stated in the public auction announcement. Moreover, this interpretation was made by the Pingxiang Municipal Planning Bureau within the scope of its functions and powers, complied with legal provisions and actual circumstances, helped to establish an image of a trustworthy government, had no significant or obvious illegal circumstances, possessed legal effect, and created a binding effect on the Municipal Land Bureau's determination regarding the land use nature. Therefore, the claim made by the Municipal Land Bureau that the land occupied by the cold storage workshop was industrial land was not supported. Yapeng Company had legitimate reasons for requesting the Municipal Land Bureau to correct the land use type in the land use certificate "Ping Guo Yong (2006) No. 43750" (land use right area of 8,359.1 square meters) to commercial and residential mixed use, and the Municipal Land Bureau should make the correction. As the transferee of the land, Yapeng Company paid the full price as agreed. The Municipal Land Bureau's demand that Yapeng Company must pay a supplementary land transfer fee if it wished to change the land use purpose lacked factual and legal basis and violated the principle of good faith.

(Judges of the Effective Judgment: Zhu Jianghong, Li Xiugui, Zou Shaoliang)

Guiding Case No. 77

Luo Rongrong v. Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau — dispute over administrative handling of price matters

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, Released on December 28, 2016)

Keywords: administrative litigation / reply to report / scope of acceptance / plaintiff standing

Ruling Gist

1. Where an administrative organ only gives an informative reply to a report that has an interest for the reporter, without handling the report in accordance with the law, such action does not fall under the category of an "act that does not have a practical impact on the rights and obligations of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations" as specified in item 6 of Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. Therefore, it is actionable and falls within the scope of acceptance of administrative lawsuits in people's courts.

2. Where a reporter reports to an administrative organ concerning the infringement of his own lawful rights and interests, he has a legal interest in the administrative organ's act of handling the report and has the standing as a plaintiff in administrative litigation.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 12 and Article 25 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC (amended on November 1, 2014)

Basic Facts

Plaintiff Luo Rongrong alleged: On May 20, 2012, when he was applying for a mobile phone number at the Ji'an Telecom business hall on Jinggangshan Avenue, Jizhou District, Ji'an City, Ji'an Telecom Company charged him a card fee of RMB 20 and issued an invoice. The plaintiff believed that Ji'an Telecom Company's charging of a card fee for the first-time application for a mobile phone number violated the prohibitive provision in the Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charging of Integrated Circuit Cards that prohibits separate charges to users. Therefore, he filed a complaint and report with the defendant, Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau, and requested that the defendant perform its statutory duty to investigate and handle the matter and provide a written reply, among other demands. Although the defendant issued a written reply, it only stated that during its investigation, the defendant found a document and part of the content of that document. The reply did not address the requests in the plaintiff's complaint and report. The defendant's act violated the relevant provisions of the Price Law of the PRC and the Provisions on the Handling of Reports of Price Violations. The plaintiff requested the court to confirm that the defendant's act in handling the plaintiff's report was unlawful, revoke the defendant's reply in accordance with the law, and order the defendant to investigate and handle the unlawful acts complained of in the plaintiff's report in accordance with the law.

Defendant Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau argued: The plaintiff's lawsuit did not comply with the relevant provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law. Administrative litigation refers to lawsuits filed by citizens, legal persons, or other organizations dissatisfied with the specific administrative acts of administrative organs. In this case, the reply made by the defendant to the plaintiff on July 3, 2012, was not a specific administrative act and was not actionable. The defendant's reply to the plaintiff complied with the procedural requirements of the Provisions on the Handling of Reports of Price Violations, and the content of the reply also informed the plaintiff of the facts verified by the defendant after investigation. The defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims in accordance with the law.

The court found through trial: On May 28, 2012, plaintiff Luo Rongrong mailed a complaint and report letter to defendant Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau, reporting that Ji'an Telecom Company had charged him a card fee of RMB 20 for the first-time application for a mobile phone SIM card. He requested that the defendant order Ji'an Telecom Company to refund the illegally collected card fee of RMB 20, investigate and confiscate all card fees collected from all telecom users for first-time SIM card applications, reward the plaintiff in accordance with the law, and provide a written reply on the relevant handling results. On May 31, 2012, the defendant received the plaintiff's complaint and report letter. On July 3, 2012, the defendant issued a "Reply on the Handling of Luo Rongrong's Complaints Letter of May 28, 2012" and mailed it to the plaintiff. The content of the reply was: "On May 31, 2012, our bureau received your complaint letter reporting that Ji'an Telecom Company charges a RMB 20 SIM card fee to users applying for new mobile phone numbers. Our bureau took this very seriously and promptly conducted an investigation. After investigation and verification, the 'Reply on the Optimization Plan for Jiangxi Telecom's Full-Service Package Tariffs' (Gan Tong Ju [2012] No. 14) jointly issued by the Jiangxi Provincial Communications Administration and the Jiangxi Provincial Development and Reform Commission stipulates: The upper limit for UIM card charges: RMB 50 per card for new subscriptions; RMB 30 per card for replacement or renewal. Our bureau is very grateful for your support and assistance to our price work." After receiving the defendant's reply, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court on the grounds that the defendant's reply was unlawful.

Judgment

The Jizhou District People's Court of Ji'an, Jiangxi Province, rendered judgment (2012) Ji Xing Chu Zi No. 13 on November 1, 2012: Quash the "Reply on the Handling of Luo Rongrong's Complaints Letter of May 28, 2012" issued by Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau, and order it to make a new written reply within fifteen days. After the judgment was announced, the parties did not appeal, and the judgment became legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: Regarding the issue of the actionability of the reply to the report by Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau. According to Article 11, paragraph 1, item 5 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law, adopted on April 4, 1989), where a person applies to an administrative organ for the performance of its statutory duty to protect personal or property rights, and the administrative organ refuses to perform or fails to reply, the people's court shall accept the lawsuit brought by the person. In this case, Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau should have investigated and determined, in accordance with the law, whether the act of Ji'an Telecom Company in charging the card fee was unlawful, and informed the plaintiff of the investigation result. However, its reply to the report merely listed the upper limit for UIM card charges stipulated in the "Reply on the Optimization Plan for Jiangxi Telecom's Full-Service Package Tariffs" (hereinafter referred to as the Reply), without stating the result of the handling of the reported matter. This act of replacing the notification of the investigation result with the notification of the relevant content of the Reply failed to perform the statutory duty to protect the reporter's property rights, and in itself constituted an infringement of Luo Rongrong's right to seek relief through proper reporting channels. It did not fall within the scope of "acts that do not have a practical impact on the rights and obligations of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations" as specified in item 6 of Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law Interpretation). Therefore, it was actionable and fell within the scope of acceptance of administrative lawsuits in people's courts.

Regarding the issue of Luo Rongrong's standing as a plaintiff. According to Articles 2, 24, paragraph 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law, and Article 12 of the Administrative Procedure Law Interpretation, a reporter who files an administrative lawsuit against the act of handling a report must have a legal interest in that act. In this case, although Luo Rongrong requested Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau to "investigate and confiscate all card fees collected from all telecom users for first-time SIM card applications in accordance with the law," this was still based on his belief that Ji'an Telecom Company's act of charging the card fee infringed upon his own lawful rights and interests. He reported the matter to Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau and held the invoice for the fee charged as evidence. Therefore, Luo Rongrong had a legal interest in the act of handling the report, had the standing as a plaintiff in administrative litigation, and could legally file an administrative lawsuit.

Regarding the legality of the reply to the report. Article 14 of the Provisions on the Handling of Reports of Price Violations stipulates: "After a report is concluded, if the reporter requests a reply and provides contact information, the price authority shall inform the reporter of the handling result in writing or orally within five working days after the conclusion." In this case, Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau, as the price authority, had the statutory duty to accept reports of price violations, examine whether the prices were unlawful, and propose categorized handling opinions. Luo Rongrong clearly listed three report requests in his complaint and report letter and requested that Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau inform him in writing of the handling result after the investigation was concluded. The reply failed to state in accordance with the law the result of the handling of the reported matter by Ji'an Municipal Price Bureau, violating the provisions of Article 14 of the Provisions on the Handling of Reports of Price Violations. It was not lawful and should be corrected.

(Judges of the Effective Judgment: Hu Jianming, Zhang Binghua, Liu Taosheng)
